matthiaskoenig/sbml4humans.summary: The python package supports Python 3.12, 3.13, 3.14 and 3.15.

The differential equations of a model are written in the native quantities of its state variables, read from the definitions to the system, and show the code of every format of sbmlode next to the math.

A report shows the differential equations of its model: the switch "Tables | Equations" writes the model as the system of ordinary differential equations it describes, every symbol linked to its element, and downloads it as code which simulates the model.
The XML of an element reads like the file in an editor: it is highlighted and stays inside the inspector, however long its lines are.

A report says what is wrong with a model: the errors and warnings of the validation of libsbml stand next to the elements they concern, and they arrive after the report, which appears as fast as before.

An annotation tells what it points to: every resource is a card with its collection, its identifier, the term of its ontology with synonyms, description and cross references, and for a ChEBI compound or a UniProt protein the information of that database. The inspector stands at the right of the…

Other tools open a model in SBML4Humans with an upload that has an address. cy3sbml, the SBML app of Cytoscape, uses it to open the model of a network with one click (cy3sbml#473). The release also closes several security gaps of the backend and of the frontend, and large reports load much faster.
A report can be read on a phone: below 768 px the report shows the tables or the inspector, one at a time, and no page scrolls sideways any more.
The tables of a report say more on less space: a value is read together with its units, and the table of the transitions of a qualitative model shows the rules instead of their number.
A maintenance release: SBML4Humans reads its models with libsbml 5.21.2. The application is the one of 0.7.0, whose notes describe the explanations of a report.

Every name a report shows explains itself. A click on the label of an attribute, on the name of a type or on the heading of a group of links opens a dialog which says what the thing is and what the specification asks of it: the data type of its value, whether it is required, what holds when a file…

A report names things as the specification does: a type is written as the name of its class and an attribute as the file writes it, so that a name which is read in a report is the name to look for in the specification, in the XML and in a library such as libsbml. The report page opens with the…

The first version of SBML4Humans on PyPI: pip install sbml4humans. The release 0.6.0 introduced the python package, but its upload was refused, so 0.6.0 exists as a GitHub release only. The application itself is the one of 0.6.0, whose notes describe the python interface and the external model…

SBML4Humans is a python package now: sbml4humans.show("model.xml") opens the report of a file of your machine in the browser, served by a local server, and the file never leaves the machine. A model of the comp package is shown with the models it is built from: an external model definition is…

SBML4Humans reads the complete data model of SBML now: the core of Level 3 and the packages comp, fbc, qual and distrib, with every reference between two objects an edge of the link graph and every object explained where it is shown. The report page is laid out anew, with the elements of a model…

SBML4Humans explains itself now: the report shows what every type, column and attribute means where it is shown, and the documentation site at matthiaskoenig.github.io/sbml4humans says what SBML is, how to load a model, how to read a report and what every element type carries.
The report of a model is now a typed data model with a link graph, and the frontend which renders it was rebuilt on Vite and Vue 3.5.
The first release of sbml4humans from its own repository. Until sbmlutils 0.10.0 the application lived in the sbmlutils repository, the backend api was sbmlutils.report.api with version 0.1.2.

matthiaskoenig/sbmlsim.summary: A release of the documentation, of quantities and of fits that converge. The documentation starts with a tutorial and shows what its code prints and plots. Results are quantities first: res.q[...], res.to(...), plots in units and label_axes. A fit simulates only the times of its data. Its finite…

A release of the speed of the simulation experiments, found with the sampling profiler of python 3.15. The experiments of a run run in a pool of worker processes, a figure is saved without drawing it twice, a formula is parsed without importing petab, and the PK analysis of the steps of the…

A patch release of three fixes of the memory and the speed: the units of a model are read without a leak of libsbml, a figure is measured with one small renderer instead of being drawn many times while it is built, and a run without observables simulates only the selections it keeps. The…

A release of the evaluation of a fit and of the first milestone of the uncertainty quantification: acceptance criteria next to the metrics, the evaluation by subsets of the data, one figure per fit mapping and better Bland-Altman plots; uncertain values with covariances, their propagation through…

A release of libroadrunner 2.11 and python 3.15: libroadrunner 2.11 fixes most of the issues sbmlsim reported upstream and is the first release with wheels for python 3.15, so sbmlsim drops the workarounds it no longer needs and compiles its models with LLJIT.
A release of the dependencies: sbmlsim does not install libroadrunner 2.11, which breaks the simulator. The simulations and the fits are unchanged.

A security release of the dependencies: the CA bundle sbmlsim reaches the network with no longer trusts the emSign root CA whose intermediate keys were compromised. The simulations and the fits are unchanged.

A release of the reports of the fits: every fit writes, without an extra command, a report of its parameter optimization that can go into the supplement of a manuscript, with the methods specific to its settings, the tables of the parameters, the data, the metrics and the provenance, the figures…
A release of the fits: a fit records what it ran with, and the Fisher information reports the relative error of a parameter. The simulations are unchanged.

A performance release: the constant parameters and the species of a model are read once per instance of roadrunner instead of on every call of sampling.parameters_of. The simulations are unchanged. The faster JIT of roadrunner, LLJIT, was measured and is not used, roadrunner 2.10 crashes with it…

A release of one feature: one legend per row, right of the grid, with the entries of all plots of the row. A figure which does not opt in does not change, apart from the position of the legend of its interactive version (see Fixes): the static images are identical to 0.9.5.

A patch release of the fixes which the port of the models of pkdb_models onto sbmlsim 0.9.4 found, and a legend outside the plots which widens only the gap right of its plot. A simulation no longer depends on whether another instance of its model is alive (every model is compiled when it is…

A patch release of fixes: the size of a compartment can be changed with a species of an assignment rule in it, which stopped every scan of the body weight of a model with such a species; a simulation of a loaded model no longer depends on the simulations which ran before it on the model, so a…

A patch release of fixes: the result of a simulation no longer depends on the simulation which ran before it on the same model, a change fires the events of a model written by sbmlutils with the right values, and a dataset reads the units with a numeric factor which PK-DB writes and converts the…

A patch release of fixes: parameter fitting, PEtab conditions and species, the models of parallel scans and of experiments, SBML events after a change, and the paths of exported problems. A few checks are stricter, they refuse input which gave wrong results silently before.
A patch release of the dependencies: pip installs the sciml extra on python 3.14 again.

A minor release built on a new scan core: Scan, Simulator and ScanResult replace ScanSim, SimulatorSerial and XResult, run the points of a scan serially or in a pool of processes, and compute observables (formulas, non-compartmental PK analyses and custom functions) from every simulation. The…

A patch release of the integrator: every state gets an absolute tolerance of its own, a model which does not read the time is integrated in local time, and every setting of the integrator reaches roadrunner. Together they remove the CVODE warning "t + h = t" after late doses and resets, which…

A patch release of the simulation engine and of the core of sbmlsim: one way to set up a simulation with the semantics of PEtab v2, PEtab v2 problems read and evaluated exactly, and a library reduced to simulating, scanning, sensitivity and uncertainty, fitting, plotting and reporting.

A patch release of the time things take: a sensitivity analysis starts its processes once and is reproducible with its seed, the SBML Test Suite runs on every core, the tests take a third of the time and a release no longer runs them again.

Units are converted in both directions, and the release notes are part of the documentation. The glimepiride example models, which have a complete unit annotation and units on numbers, all convert to valid CellML and simulate with libopencor now.

matthiaskoenig/libsbgn-python.summary: This is a security release: the emSign root certificates, whose intermediate keys were compromised, are no longer trusted.

This release follows the latest SBGN specifications (PD L1V2.1, ER L1V2.0, AF L1V1.2) and validates documents against the rules of the specifications: the rules the schema cannot express, and the schematron rules of the SBGN languages, as the Java library libSBGN does.

This release contains the changes of 0.6.4, which was tagged but not published: the release workflow pinned the PyPI publish action to a commit without a container image. 0.6.5 is the first release with these changes on PyPI.
Python 3.15 support, with test coverage on Linux, macOS and Windows.

every change goes into develop through a pull request; the tests, ruff, ty and the documentation build have to pass before a merge is possible · the master branch is renamed to main, which tracks the latest published release and is fast-forwarded to the released commit by the release workflow…
